rule_objections: No stated rule exists for Erlang; I applied: functions, modules, types/records, top-level constants. Including -type and -module as expected is a judgement; a developer looking up a record or type by name would expect it.
findings: Only functions are extracted: 91 of 91 function names (clause groups folded per name/arity) are right, with no spurious functions. Nothing else is: no -module, no 22 -type/-opaque, no -define constants, and the three -record declarations come out as kind function.
The 5 -callback declarations in cowboy_websocket.erl are also not recorded; I did not count them as expected because the default rule is silent on behaviours.
Erlang has no fixtures directory (judged good earlier); on types, modules and records it is not good.
not_done: Function expectations were checked by clause grouping with a script whose arity counter is inexact on binary patterns; I reconciled the six differences by reading the clauses.
